summary: Define the case-study question and scope
purpose: Keep the independent study focused on a decision supported by public evidence.
acceptance: Question, Steam-only scope and limits are stated in the case study.

purpose: Make the event-window comparisons traceable and repeatable.
acceptance: Sources, complete windows, alternative baselines and competing events are documented.
rationale: Protects the validity of the proposal.

purpose: Turn the results into a clear recommendation and supporting project documentation.
acceptance: Case-study PDF, Power BI report and linked Jira/Confluence documentation are available.

purpose: Ask whether patch-to-Warbond spacing was associated with later Steam activity.
acceptance: Question, audience, eight-release scope and feasible public-data decision are written down.
rationale: Avoids building a dashboard without a decision.

purpose: Separate daily buckets from intraday samples.
acceptance: Raw snapshot has a hash, schema, date profile and benchmark check.
rationale: Every activity metric depends on the grain.

purpose: Keep the analysis timing and sample selection clear.
acceptance: Study is identified as retrospective. The eight-release sample and windows are stated; no preregistered hypothesis is claimed.

summary: Document daily grouping and timezone limits
purpose: Explain which exported player values support daily comparisons.
acceptance: Historical daily peaks and recent sampled maxima are distinguished. The missing timezone metadata and provisional UTC interpretation are disclosed.
rationale: Could change daily alignment and eligibility.

purpose: Save official news, wiki history and review histogram.
acceptance: Manifest, hashes and source-specific filters resolve to local snapshots.

summary: Check patch and Warbond dates against official posts
purpose: Use release dates rather than announcement publication dates.
acceptance: Eight Warbonds have news IDs, date cues and saved sources. Scheduled availability and same-day availability are distinguished.

summary: Check event windows and alternative baselines
purpose: Make missing observations and baseline sensitivity visible.
acceptance: All eight cases have complete main windows. Seven- and 28-day baselines and pre-patch-sequence anchors are compared; no sampled maxima substitute for daily peaks.
rationale: Separates defensible results from missing observations.

summary: Review nearby releases and other explanations
purpose: Avoid attributing all activity changes to the release gap.
acceptance: September and December content, overlapping updates, existing trends and the small sample are discussed.

summary: Compare investigation options and select content timing
purpose: Choose an investigation that can be completed using the available evidence.
acceptance: Content timing is compared with loadout viability and policy communication. The selected direction and its limits are recorded; no invented effort scores are used.

purpose: Translate the mixed timing results into a practical planning review.
acceptance: Recommendation specifies launch, weekly and days 22-35 checks, comparable content and overlapping-release notes. Future team implementation is distinguished from completed analysis.
rationale: Prevents an aggregate trend from being treated as a retention result.

summary: Build and check the two-page Power BI report
purpose: Present the eight-release activity and timing comparisons in Power BI web.
acceptance: Page one shows launch and later changes for eight Warbonds. Page two has an eight-row table and eight scatter points. Percentages, labels and the two-page PDF export are checked.

purpose: Explain the findings and recommendation in a concise standalone submission.
acceptance: Four-page PDF compiles from LaTeX, includes source and Drive links, and describes the completed analysis and its limits.

summary: Publish Confluence pages and link the Jira work
purpose: Keep the findings, decisions and delivery status together.
acceptance: Confluence parent and five child pages are published, evidence is linked, Jira keys are recorded and the board reflects verified completion. Recipient access is checked before sharing.
rationale: Only approved material should be shared.
